thread:
mike: Quick thread — thinking about lowering exporter egress by combining per-route head sampling with budgeted tail sampling per-tenant. Sketch below. PTAL @anika @sara

anika: Sounds promising. Concern: tail sampling needs access to full traces to decide -> means we still pull spans upstream for a bit. How do we avoid OOM / queue pressure?

lee: We can keep a short local ring buffer for trace fragments (configurable size) + probabilistic early-drop for noisy routes. Then forward candidate trace ids to the tail-sampler service for full fetch.

mike: Exactly. Proposal: two-phase exporter pipeline so we don't always ship full spans. Phase A: cheap prefix exporter (headers + error tags + a couple spans). Phase B: tail sampler requests trace payloads on demand. Example config snippet below:

mike: ```yaml
sampling:
  routes:
    - name: '/v1/generate'
      head_rate: 0.01 # cheap prefix sampling
      tail_budget_per_min: 200 # max full traces/min
      retention_tier: bronze
  default_tail_policy: budgeted
  buffer_size: 1000
```

sara: Will this integrate with our current OTLP receivers (batcher/backpressure)? We already rely on exporter flow-control and retries. Need clear semantics for when we pull full traces vs. decline.

telemetry-bot: FYI our otlp-recv already exposes per-connection flow control. Suggest adding a `x-sample-hint: tail-candidate` header on the prefix exporter and new metric `sampling.buffer_drops` + `sampling.tail_fetch_retries`.

anika: UX question: how do we present this to customers in Console? Per-route sampling rates + retention tiers (gold/silver/bronze) feels obvious, but we should surface expected bytes saved and a simple SLO slider so teams understand tradeoffs.

lee: Also quota/billing implications: if a customer opts into gold retention for a route we blow past their bytes quota. Might be simpler to default to a budgeted retention and let teams increase budgets per-route. That way billing aligns with explicit budget consumption.

mike: Rollout plan idea: A/B enable this for a small subset of routes (and a handful of tenants) -> measure exporter_bytes, tail_sample_rate, buffer_drops, and P99_trace_latency for error detection. Dashboard metrics to include: exporter_bytes_total, sampling.tail_fetch_count, sampling.buffer_drops, trace_error_recall.

sara: Can we optimize the heuristic to avoid full trace fetch in many cases? e.g., tail-sample on `http.status_code >= 500` or `span.tags.error=true` first, then expand to anomaly heuristics.

anika: Agreed. Start with tag heuristics + budgeted sampling. ML anomaly sampler later once we have labels. Don't want to ship ML before infra can explain decisions.

lee: One more infra note: need a fallback_exporter path if the tail-sampler is down (fail-open vs fail-closed debate). I vote fail-open but with strong alerts and quota safety (e.g., throttled fallback).

mike: Good point. For safety, fail-open but drop full-fetches and set a temporary head_rate=0.1 for 5m so we get some visibility. Also record a `sampling.fallback_triggered` event.

anika: Console ownership? I can take the UI/UX work (route controls + budget slider).

sara: I can own infra changes (OTLP changes, buffer, metrics). Ping when you open the RFC. :thumbsup:

mike: I'll draft an RFC with config schema, metrics, rollout and an A/B test plan. Will tag @anika and @sara when draft PR is ready.
